title: How many horses are really in the king's stable?
description: Farhan reads the king's horse story and the video finds the caretaker's counting slip: a corner horse is counted on two sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: a corner horse belongs to two sides, so adding the sides counts it twice. Watch for children who trust four sides of five and say twenty.

source: The caretaker says 5 horses on each of 4 sides makes 20. One
video_script.why: The child has read the story but has not yet seen that a corner horse is counted once for each side it stands on.
video_script.substitution: Add the counts of the four sides, then take away one for every corner horse that was counted twice.
video_script.anchor: Farhan at his desk reading the king's horse story, with the square stable drawn from above
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu adds the four sides of five horses and says twenty, forgetting that the corner horse sits in two of the rows.

final_answer.value: 19 horses, because the corner horse was counted twice
final_answer.spoken: nineteen horses, because the corner horse was counted twice

maths_rules: one corner horse is on two sides, so it is counted twice, 1 extra count
slip: saying 20 horses forgets the corner horse is counted twice
your turn: 4 sides with 8 plants each, 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32 counted; one corner plant counted twice; 32 - 1 = 31 plants; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: a corner horse is counted on two sides. Wrong idea: four sides of five make twenty horses. A square stable seen from above stays on the stage; the sums go on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>The twenty came from counting every side separately.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>In this stable one horse stands at a corner, so it is counted twice. We take away one.
<bookmark mark='minus'/>Twenty take away one leaves nineteen.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>There are only nineteen horses, because the corner horse was counted twice.
